title: Customer POC Staged Rollout Timeline & Stakeholder Commitments
content:
Overview:
This document outlines a staged rollout plan for the ACME legal-assistant POC, covering workshop agenda, milestone timeline, stakeholder commitments, ownership of deliverables, quick risk register, and acceptance criteria. The goal is a controlled 4-week production-like trial in customer environment (VPC) using Redwood Private with observability hooks and fallback model pairs.

Context and goals:
- Customer: ACME Corp (legal automation pilot)
- Primary objective: Validate Redwood Private in-customer VPC, measure latency/throughput for 1k daily users surrogate load, and demonstrate graceful degradation (fallback models + cache) while retaining answer quality for legal Q&A.
- Secondary objective: Validate deployment automation (terraform + rollout policies) and integrate customer logging/KMS for audit.
- Success metric: 95th percentile end-to-end latency < 400ms for typical prompts; no loss of signal on the eval prompt set (>92% pass on quality regression tests); zero sensitive-data leakage incidents.

High-level phased plan (4 weeks):
Phase 0 — Preflight (week -1 to day 0):
- Deliverables: VPC peering checklist, KMS access validated, sample dataset sanitized, basic Terraform exec plan.
- Owners: Solutions Eng (Avery) / Customer Infra (ACME infra lead)
- Key open items: customer firewall rules (TODO: ACME to confirm), KMS role mapping (TODO: security to validate).

Phase 1 — Workshop & Quickstart (day 1–3):
- Day 1: Kickoff + security walkthrough (SRE + security). Objectives: trust boundary, network flow, audit log retention.
- Day 2: Model choice & prompt engineering workshop. Run Redwood Optimize quick-scan to recommend quantization/batching profile.
- Day 3: Baseline eval run & acceptance criteria alignment.
- Outputs: workshop recording, chosen model variant, baseline latency/cost estimates.

Phase 2 — Canary Deployment (week 1):
- Deploy dedicated VMs/GPUs in customer VPC with 10% traffic routing from sandbox domain.
- Tasks: instrumentation hooks for per-request trace IDs, enable prefix caching for common legal templates, set SLOs in Console (95/99 latency targets).
- Owners: Eng-deploy (Morgan), Observability (Jordan), Customer Eng contact for traffic steering.

Phase 3 — Surge Test & Monitoring (week 2):
- Run synthetic surge (burst to 2x expected load), measure tail latency, token costs, caching hit rate.
- Validate fallback pairing: when primary model CPU/GPU under high queue depth, route to lower-cost quantized variant with metadata noting potential quality delta.
- Escalation path: if SLO breach > 15 minutes, auto-fallback to Hosted API and page on-call SRE.

Phase 4 — Customer UAT & Handoff (week 3):
- Enable real user traffic under monitoring with canary to full 100% if metrics stable.
- Conduct final training for customer ops: cost dashboards, model pinning, canary rollback.
- Deliverables: runbook for traffic ramp, handoff checklist, post-mortem template.

Phase 5 — Close & Learn (week 4):
- Collect evals, run quality regression on customer prompt set, produce final SLI/SLO report and recommendations for production.
- Proposal: recommended Dedicated capacity sizing and pricing estimate based on observed QPS and token rates.

Stakeholders & RACI (summary):
- Customer project lead: Maria Gonzalez — R
- Solutions Eng lead: Avery Chen — A
- Observability: Jordan Patel — C
- Deploy/Infra: Morgan Rivera — R/C
- Security/compliance: Sophie Martínez — C
- Account Exec: Ethan Brooks — I
Notes: R = Responsible, A = Approver, C = Consulted, I = Informed. Confirm names and escalation contacts during kickoff.

Task tracker (selected tasks — expand in Jira):
- Preflight network test (owner: Morgan) — due: 2025-11-10 — status: todo
- Generate sanitized eval set (owner: ACME data lead) — due: 2025-11-07 — status: in_progress
- Infra terraform module for VPC + GPU (owner: Morgan) — due: 2025-11-14 — status: todo
- Observability dashboard template (owner: Jordan) — due: 2025-11-12 — status: todo
- Workshop slide deck + prompt examples (owner: Avery) — due: 2025-11-05 — status: done
- Canary routing policy (owner: Solutions Eng) — due: 2025-11-18 — status: todo

Quick risk register (top 6):
- Network isolation misconfig: High — Mitigation: preflight network test + dry run of peering, block public egress until validated.
- KMS permission delays: Medium — Mitigation: escalate to customer security early, offer temporary sample keys for sandbox with strict TTL.
- Quality regression when using quantized model: Medium-High — Mitigation: run side-by-side evals, keep canary traffic low until tolerance validated.
- Latency SLO breach under burst: High — Mitigation: configure automatic fallback + autoscale policy; pre-provision burst capacity.
- Observability gaps (missing traces): Medium — Mitigation: add mandatory trace-id header and validate during canary.
- Billing surprise for customer: Medium — Mitigation: enable token-level cost dashboard and set hard quota alerts.

Workshop agenda (detailed — day 2 example):
- 09:00–09:20: Recap objectives + constraints (Avery)
- 09:20–10:00: Model variants and quantization tradeoffs (Applied ML)
- 10:00–10:30: Prompt engineering patterns for legal domain (Solutions Eng)
- 10:30–11:00: Coffee + breakout to draft 10 canonical prompts (customer + SE)
- 11:00–12:00: Redwood Optimize run & interpretation (Jordan)
- 12:00–13:00: Lunch
- 13:00–15:00: Hands-on deploy and small-load run in customer sandbox (Morgan)
- 15:00–16:00: Discuss rollback, canary thresholds, and runbook glue (SRE + Customer Ops)
- 16:00–16:30: Action items & next steps alignment

Acceptance criteria (min bar):
- Canary runs for 48h with no critical incidents and SLO breaches < 15 minutes total.
- Eval pass rate >= 92% on customer prompt set comparing baseline and canary model.
- Traceability: every request has trace + cost attribution captured in console.
- Security: KMS integration validates with at-rest encryption and audit logs collected in central SIEM.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm whether ACME requires FIPS 140-2 HSM for KMS (Sophie to confirm).
- Decide on retention window for request logs (customer prefers 90 days — cost implications).
- Build small synthetic traffic harness that mimics legal template bursts (Morgan to prototype).
- Pre-authorize temporary Hosted API fallback keys for emergency routing.

Appendix: quick checklist for go/no-go at end of Canary week:
- [ ] All infra checks green (network, KMS, firewall)
- [ ] Observability dashboards show correct metrics (latency, qps, cache-hit rate)
- [ ] Quality regression < 8% delta vs baseline
- [ ] Customer ops trained on rollback and pinning

Notes and context (informal):
- This doc is intentionally lightweight and workshop-forward — expand items into Jira tasks and add the sprint board before day 1.
- Expect changes after the initial workshop; keep this file as the single source for stakeholder commitments until replaced by the engagement playbook.

Action: Review before kickoff (Avery action) and bring the network diagram to the preflight meeting.
